correctness.rationale: For all 256 local rules, the 4- and 16-state transfer graph edge constraints exactly characterize Fix(F) and Fix(F²) at every cyclic length, including n=1,2. A marked edge lies on a directed cycle exactly when its endpoints share a strong component, yielding an all-length nonexistence test. Independent exhaustive length-1..6 search agreed with the SCC test for every rule: 107 negatives, 149 positives with twelve first witnesses at six. Exact SymPy characteristic polynomials give 23/40/51 distinct denominators/pairs and a separate direct update check matched the formal traces for all 2304 rule-length cases; the complete 256-row table was checked. The finite rule universe is fully covered, and no infinite assertion depends only on the nine-length brute force.

originality.rationale: The exact 256-rule joint two-iterate rational-zeta census and sharp six-site existence cutoff are not contained in the inspected full scientific statements. A published Rule 18 result and an owned Rule 73 result cover only individual rules; a published eight-site language test studies one-update image membership, not temporal return. The older Banks–Djirar and modern Koller–Hudcová methods anticipate transfer graphs but not the full table. The most relevant broader classification of Epperlein computes other topological periodic-point invariants and remains a historical-risk source; partial access and unindexed prior tables explicitly qualify priority.

Older cellular-automaton cycle-count compilations might be unindexed, particularly for the qualitative 107-rule no-cycle partition.
Graph methods and the trace–determinant identity are established prior art and are not claimed as new.

value.rationale: The complete natural 256-rule universe admits a surprising and sharp global first-temporal-two witness bound of six sites, with twelve sharp rule witnesses and a rigorously excluded 107-rule family. A simple short-ring enumeration alone would not prove this; the 16-state directed-cycle criterion extends absence to all ring lengths. The exact 23/40/51 rational zeta classification determines every fixed and period-two configuration count for all spatial lengths, a substantive new exact dynamical invariant table beyond single-rule counts and not an arbitrarily selected computational slice.
